agree.reason: The $49,000 figure, set against the $47,000 the town gave last time, and the $7.50-per-resident framing would likely win over a doubtful former donor, though this reader gets no reopening date or spending report to tip a larger pledge.

honest.reason: Every number is accurate and none is invented, but the $85,000 roof cost is stated as firm even though the estimate could rise by up to 15%, and calling all-or-nothing 'the same promise' stretches what last time was a refund after the campaign fell short.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out the $36,000 already committed, the $49,000 still needed, that this is only $2,000 more than last time, about $7.50 per resident and the 76-mile round trip, all in their most persuasive true form.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately: the screen stays dark, the nearest cinema stays 38 miles away and the bank pledge and lease are lost, though it doesn't put the 180 weekly tickets to use as lost demand.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition names the amount ($85,000), the date (June 30) and the consequence (every pledge returned in full), but the risk of the roof cost rising goes unmentioned.

objections.reason: It meets the failed-campaign objection head on, but it offers no quarterly spending report, no reopening date and nothing for a reader who has just given to the ambulance fund, and the 'planning beyond opening night' paragraph is thin.

fit.reason: At roughly 310 words, it is a signed, well-paragraphed crowdfunding pitch under the 350-word limit.
